anti_overlap: fd-forcing-curve-historiography owns whether print->broadcast->algorithmic belongs on the global century forcing curves vs. a per-country StructuralProfile axis, a question about WHICH SLOW-CLOCK HOST carries the era transition, not which population tier consumes it; fd-calibration-reproof-economics owns costing the actual referee/certification burden of whatever mechanism is chosen, not whether it is tier-correct. Concede historiographical and certification-cost questions to those agents; own only the population-tier-locality and agent-vs-country conservation-duplication question.
decision_lens: A medium-form or flow-conserving effect can be implemented as a per-country scalar (StructuralProfile axis), a per-institution-agent state update (ideology/personality/goal layer, gated by SHADOWBENCH_DISABLE_AGENT_EFFECTS), or both — and each placement has different conservation semantics, different referee cost, and a different answer to 'does disabling this ablation flag actually turn it off.' An agent whose personality facets or ideology distance are what actually consume media-form input (e.g. a medium's epistemic ceiling bends how an agent's conviction updates, not just a country-level narrative_coherence ceiling) has a real claim to being the correct host; a design that only ever touches StructuralProfile without asking whether the ~80 agents should read or write the same state is not choosing the cheap tier, it is skipping a tier entirely. Conversely, forcing this into the agent tier when the effect is really a population-level aggregate (like current country pressure families) manufactures per-agent free parameters (31 personality facets x ~80 agents) that the referee never asked to re-prove and that the B7 lesson would flag as a needless multiplication of state.
focus: Whether a medium/modality effect that modulates existing couplings belongs at the agent tier (per-agent ideology/personality state, ~80 institutional agents) rather than, or in addition to, the country tier, and whether putting it at the wrong tier breaks either the conservation accounting or the ablation/referee contract
name: fd-agent-based-modeling-tier-locality
persona: Apply the perspective of an agent-based-modeling practitioner specializing in multi-level model design — the discipline of deciding, for any candidate mechanism, which population tier (individual agent, institution, region, aggregate) is the correct locus of state and update, given that effects computed at the wrong tier either wash out under aggregation, double-count against an aggregate-tier analog, or become invisible to the tier's own ablation switch.
review_areas: Whether the fused mechanism sketch states, for each candidate coupling-modulation, which tier (country/StructuralProfile, institution-agent/ideology-personality, or both) owns the new or modulated state, and whether that choice is justified by where the effect actually operates rather than by which tier was easiest to write about

Whether AGENT_EFFECT_SCALE=0.05 and the existing action-effect pipeline (tick/effects.rs) is treated as the natural agent-tier host for a medium-modulation multiplier, or whether the sketch invents a parallel per-agent mechanism that duplicates it

Whether SHADOWBENCH_DISABLE_AGENT_EFFECTS actually gates any proposed agent-tier medium effect at the same point it gates existing agent effects (effects.rs:146-148, application only — agents still tick and consume RNG identically), or whether the sketch's ablation story would leave agents ticking on media-modulated state even with the flag set, silently breaking byte-identical-when-disabled

Whether a medium/modality effect proposed at BOTH tiers (country ceiling AND agent conviction-update bending) has an explicit non-double-counting argument — the two tiers must modulate disjoint quantities or one must be derived from the other, not independently re-spend the same conserved head

Whether agent ideology-distance (diplomacy pillar) or agent personality-facet evolution is plausibly the correct host for the 'digital reversal' tetrad effect (a channel that empowered an agent's goals flipping to undermine them) in a way a country-level scalar cannot represent, given agents already carry memory (20 entries) and condition-to-action rules that a per-country axis has no analog for

Whether adding tier-crossing state (a per-agent read of a per-country medium scalar, or vice versa) introduces a new coupling edge that itself needs referee re-proof, and whether that edge is costed in the sketch or silently assumed free

severity_examples.condition: No single-source-of-truth statement for the modulation quantity across tiers; the conservation ledger required by the river-hydraulics half of the fuse is falsified by tier duplication, not by a single-tier bug
severity_examples.scenario: The mechanism sketch proposes a medium-modulation effect that writes to both a per-country StructuralProfile axis and a per-agent ideology/personality field from the same upstream signal, with no accounting for which one is authoritative, so total modulated head is applied twice against the same conserved budget

severity_examples.condition: Violates the B7/Gibson calibration discipline's default-off, byte-identical-when-disabled requirement specifically at the agent tier, where the existing ablation precedent (gate only the final application) is not followed
severity_examples.scenario: A proposed agent-tier effect (e.g. medium-form bending how fast an institution's conviction updates) is wired into the agent tick loop but not into the SHADOWBENCH_DISABLE_AGENT_EFFECTS gate, so agent RNG streams or state diverge with the flag set even though existing agent effects remain byte-identical when disabled

severity_examples.condition: No agent-tier alternative considered or explicitly costed-and-rejected for any of the mechanism candidates, despite the target document naming agent-tier media effects as one of the three regions that must be covered
severity_examples.scenario: The sketch defaults every candidate mechanism to the country tier without ever asking whether the ~80-agent ideology/personality layer is the cheaper or more theory-faithful host, missing that agent memory and condition-action rules could express McLuhan's 'reversal' (a medium that served an agent's goals begins working against them) more directly than a country scalar

success_hints: Reward an explicit tier-assignment table across the sketch's candidate mechanisms: country/StructuralProfile vs institution-agent/ideology-personality vs both-with-a-stated-authority-rule

Reward identification of tick/effects.rs and AGENT_EFFECT_SCALE as the concrete integration point for any agent-tier medium effect, with a stated ablation-gate location matching the existing effects.rs:146-148 precedent

Reward a concrete answer to whether agent-tier media effects change tipping-country genealogy or T0 timing in ways a country-tier-only design cannot, since that is the actual bar for adding tier-crossing state under the referee's scarce re-proof budget
Penalize any treatment of 'agent tier vs country tier' as a stylistic choice rather than a conservation-and-ablation-cost question with a right answer per mechanism

Penalize a sketch that mentions the ~80 agents only to note they exist, without engaging whether ideology distance or personality-facet evolution is the correct host for any specific tetrad effect (enhance/obsolesce/retrieve/reverse)
task_context: Design a conservation-aware media-ecology mechanism for shadow-work: fuse the medium-form lens (fd-media-ecology-medium-bias) with the conserved-flow lens (fd-river-hydraulics-flow-coupling) into a 'modulate, don't inject' mechanism sketch, and cover the three unreached regions: agent-tier media effects, print→broadcast→algorithmic as a century forcing curve, and referee re-proof costing
